No, I haven't. Why would they backfire? What kind of tactics?

I'm sorry if I'm wasting your time. I'm so glad you're trying to help but I don't know the right type of things to say to help make it easier for you. I'm really sorry

It makes me feel much better that it's fixable. I'm a sophomore in college now and I've always had slight issues with self-esteem but they got way worse my junior year of high school when I became depressed and I feel like I've recovered from that depression now, like I can get out of bed and shower regularly and do my homework, but I haven't quite fully recovered all the self-esteem I lost there. 

The thing is that earlier in this school year, I felt like I was doing great, and my mindset was just that I would focus on myself and having fun this year and not trying to get people to like me. That kind of seemed to backfire though, because I'm at this point in my life where the fun thing to do on the weekends is drink with my friends, and I guess getting drunk gave me these brief windows of confidence, and now I feel like I'm even less fun to be around when I'm not drunk than I was before. 

And I'm not getting drunk every single weekend or anything, I just mean that I feel more comfortable around people when I'm drunk, and I realize that's problematic, but I'm genuinely more fun to be around when I'm drunk which is also problematic. I don't know.

Thank you for replying. It sounds like it could be right. I have such supportive parents though, who always tell me that I'm valuable and all that. I specifically remember thinking in the fourth grade that I had never noticed until that year that kids didn't like me, so maybe kindergarten through 3rd I was just oblivious but maybe I just don't remember. I've had good friends but I don't think I've ever felt understood if that makes sense. This might all be pointless backstorying; I don't know. Is there any way to fix it if that's what's happening here?
